A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Obscuro research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, Table 1, and complete appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original matches against ZS21 and human players, plus ablations, time-scaling experiments, self-play statistics, and gameplay analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the 85.1% score against ZS21, 80% against the top human, and appendix self-play analyses.

M1.justification: KLUSS, one-sided GT-CFR, PCFR+, Resolve weighting, Stockfish evaluation, and purification are unchanged. The detailed algorithms and pseudocode match across versions; expanded main-text descriptions explain existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Fog of War chess coverage: AI opponents, humans of varying strength, the top human, self-play, and random play. No new task, population, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ZS21, the same ablated agents, simple-eval Obscuro, and the random opponent. v2 clarifies ablation opponents and abbreviates simple-eval as SE without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4 additionally summarizes the top-human match in Elo (+241), extending the metrics reported for that comparison. Game counts and time controls remain unchanged; the newly stated two-day schedule documents the existing match rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations, weaker-evaluation experiment, time scaling, random-opponent check, and gameplay analyses are retained. v1 Appendices D–E move into v2 Sections 4.1–4.2, while v1 Appendix C becomes Appendix E; these are existing analyses.

E5.justification: v1 confines its blanket z > 5 statement to Appendix D's ablations. v2 explicitly extends that statement to all results in Sections 4.1–4.2, including the weaker-evaluation and time-scaling experiments. This expands significance reporting without establishing additional runs or a changed testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds the +241 Elo summary for the unchanged 16–4 top-human match and reports its binomial p-value as 0.0118 instead of 0.011. Match counts, scores, ablation results, time-scaling results, computational statistics, and Table 1 values otherwise match.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its proof already appear in v1 Appendix B.3.3 and are retained in v2 Appendix C.4. Formal subgame definitions and king-versus-king arguments remain unchanged in substance; the latter receive explanatory clarifications about safe and adjacent moves.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows both largest-game claims to zero-sum games, although the introduction and conclusion retain broader wording. The conclusion also removes the categorical claim that no large-scale computation was required to learn a value function or blueprint. The central superhuman-performance claim remains.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning search, evaluation quality, bluffing, risk-taking, and first-mover advantage are retained. So are limitations concerning KLUSS safety, Stockfish-based evaluation, infoset storage, and failure to exploit weak opponents. Moving the safety caveat from a footnote into the main text changes its prominence.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that the top-human match comprised ten games on each of two days, allowing overnight analysis. It explicitly identifies the default ablation opponent and explains the contents and viewing perspective of the existing game-record links. Hardware, implementation parameters, and pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Solinas et al. (2023), History filtering in imperfect information games: algorithms and complexity, and connects its worst-case intractability results to the common-knowledge discussion in Section 2. Other research positioning is largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: appendix experiments become main-text Sections 4.1–4.2, and the technical appendix is separated into notation, method details, and hardware sections. Numerous generic supplementary-material references become precise cross-references, several footnotes become prose, and citations switch to author–year style. Author information and explanatory wording are also revised.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains the missing distance labels 1, 2, 3, and infinity. The unchanged time-scaling plot moves from appendix Figure 7 to main-text Figure 3, with corresponding figure renumbering and float relocation. Front matter and page layout are adjusted, while the remaining visual content and table structure are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes existing evidence easier to find, fixes Figure 2's missing explanatory labels, and clarifies human-match and ablation details. These provide a limited improvement in readability and transparency without substantial new validation. The abstract's narrower claims improve precision, although their inconsistent wording elsewhere remains unresolved.
